description:
Get how the site does in search results over a window: per search query, its clicks, impressions and average position, with the window's totals and, with `compare_to`, their change against an earlier window. Use `well_list_daily_metrics` for raw daily rows.

`totals` cover the whole window whatever the `limit`: never add query rows to get a total. They are the sums of the query rows the search source returns, so they are lower than the totals of the Search Console chart: Google leaves out rare queries, returns at most 50,000 rows a day, and only web results are read. Say so when you compare them with Search Console. `average_position` is computed (the sum of positions divided by the impressions; 1 is the top result): never average it yourself. `changes.<figure>` gives `absolute` (current minus earlier) and `share` (a fraction of the earlier value: 0.12 is +12 %), null when the earlier value is 0 or missing. A lower average position is a better one.

Search Console publishes its data two to three days late. `window` ends on the last day a source stored when that day is before the end of `requested_window`: say which days were read. `comparison_window` has as many days as `window`, except a whole calendar quarter, which compares with the whole previous quarter, and `same_days_last_year` across 29 February.

`queries` are sorted by clicks, then impressions. With `position_from` or `position_to`, only the queries whose average position falls in that range, both ends included, sorted by impressions. `has_more` is true when more queries match: say the list is cut.

A search source is one connection, and two connections are never added: `totals_by_source` lists each. One connection can read several Search Console properties (a domain property and a URL-prefix property, or two sites), and its figures then mix them: rows of two properties that share a query, day, device and country keep only one of the two values, so the figure is neither property's figure nor their sum. Sales per query are not available yet: `paid_orders`, `real_sales`, `landing_pages` and `shares_landing_page` are always null, and `pages` is empty, because the search source stores no query-to-page rows. Say so, and never estimate them. A null figure was not measured, never zero: `missing` says why. `no_source_rows` (no search source reported the window), `several_search_sources` (two or more connections reported the window, so the figures are per source only), `not_attributable` (the search source stores no query-to-page rows, so no paid order reaches a query), `ga4_not_connected` (the key events a search brought come from Google Analytics).

`search_sources` lists every live search connection, even one that stored nothing, with `synced_at`, `last_reported_date` (the last day it stored in the window) and `fresh_enough` (synced within the day and, for Search Console, data up to at most three days before today). When a source is not fresh enough, say its figures may be incomplete, and offer `well_request_sync` with its id.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

compare_to.description: Compare to an earlier window. previous_period: the same number of days just before the window, for yesterday, the last N days and two named dates; a quarter window compares to the previous quarter from its first day instead: a whole quarter to the whole previous quarter, and a quarter to date to the same span three months earlier, its last day clamped to the end of a shorter month (1 October to 2 November compares to 1 July to 2 August). same_days_last_year: the same calendar days one year earlier (29 February reads as 28 February).

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

limit.description: Queries to return, at most 200. Default 50.

position_from.description: The first position of the average position range, included; 1 is the top result.

position_to.description: The last position of the average position range, included; 1 is the top result.

window.description: The days to read. The result states the requested dates in `requested_window` and the days read in `window`.

oneOf.description: The last `days` days, ending yesterday in the workspace's time zone.

from_date.description: The first day, as YYYY-MM-DD, included.

to_date.description: The last day; the window holds at most 180 days, both ends included, as YYYY-MM-DD, included.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_get_search_performance

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.

title: Get search performance
